draft.briefing: Hey, you're on MG Road! Known as South Parade before independence, it was renamed Mahatma Gandhi Road on 26 February 1948 and is still one of the busiest roads in Bengaluru.
draft.hungryLine: Grab a late night tea at Savera on MG Road, or head to Residency Road for biryani and Death by Chocolate.

moodReplies.show-me-around: Brigade Road is a 3 minute walk, Church Street is 4 minutes away, and St. Mark's Cathedral is about 12 minutes on foot.
moodReplies.somewhere-to-chill: Wander Church Street, the first street in the city paved with granite cobblestones.
moodReplies.surprise-me: Jawaharlal Nehru, Queen Elizabeth II and Nikita Khrushchev have all eaten at Koshy's, a 9 minute walk from here.

spots.name: Church Street

spots.name: St. Mark's Cathedral
spots.detail: 12 min walk · English Baroque church from 1808

legends.title: The martyr's church
legends.body: St. Andrew's was consecrated in memory of Mary Elizabeth McGoun, and was once known as the martyr's church. Her monument is at the end of the altar.

tips.title: Ring in New Year on Church Street.
tips.body: It's one of the city's popular New Year's Eve celebration spots.

tips.title: Take the metro.
tips.body: MG Road and Trinity stations are both right on the road.

story.title: St. Mark's Cathedral
story.body: The cathedral at the west end of the road was founded, inspired by St Paul's Cathedral.

story.title: St. Andrew's Church
story.body: The Scottish kirk on Cubbon Road was consecrated.

story.title: A new name
story.body: South Parade became Mahatma Gandhi Road on 26 February 1948.

story.title: The metro comes
story.body: MG Road metro station opened on 20 October 2011, linking east and west Bengaluru.

story.title: Cobblestones on Church Street
story.body: Church Street was repaved in granite cobblestones laid in a Kasuti pattern, a nod to Karnataka's heritage.
